title: What the $25,000 CSLB Contractor Bond Covers in California
dek: California's $25,000 contractor bond protects homeowners and unpaid employees. If it is canceled or paid out, your license can be suspended.
keyPoints: The contractor's bond has been $25,000 since January 1, 2023, under SB 607.
Homeowners damaged by license law violations and employees owed wages can claim against it.
A bond is canceled 30 days after CSLB receives the cancellation notice; without a replacement, the license is suspended.
LLCs also need a $100,000 worker bond and at least $1 million in liability insurance for five or fewer members.
Work done while a license is suspended counts as unlicensed work.
body: Every active California contractor license needs a $25,000 contractor's bond on file with the Contractors State License Board. The $25,000 amount took effect January 1, 2023, under Senate Bill 607. CSLB describes the bond as filed for the benefit of consumers damaged by defective construction or other license law violations, and of employees who were not paid wages owed to them.

Who can make a claim. According to CSLB, homeowners, anyone damaged by a willful and deliberate violation of a construction contract, and employees damaged by a contractor's failure to pay wages can file claims. Claimants go directly to the surety company, which they can find through the Contractor's Bond History link on your license detail page. CSLB does not process bond claims; it investigates license complaints separately.

Why it is different from insurance. The surety pays valid claims, but under a typical surety agreement the contractor is expected to repay the surety. Read your indemnity agreement so you know what you signed, and talk with your bond agent or attorney if a claim arrives.

Bond of qualifying individual: $25,000, required when your qualifier is a Responsible Managing Employee, or a Responsible Managing Officer who owns less than 10% of the voting stock. Each qualifier must meet the requirement.

LLC worker bond: LLC licenses need a $100,000 surety bond in addition to the $25,000 contractor bond. LLCs also need liability insurance with a cumulative limit of at least $1 million for five or fewer personnel of record, plus $100,000 for each additional member, up to $5 million.
Disciplinary bond: if CSLB orders one, it is at least $25,000 and up to ten times the contractor bond, and it must stay on file for at least two years.

How bond problems turn into suspensions. CSLB lists several triggers: the surety cancels the bond, a judgment or claim payment reduces the bond below the required amount, the surety loses its authorization with the California Department of Insurance, or an RMO's ownership drops below 10%. A bond is canceled 30 days from the date CSLB receives the cancellation notice, and if no replacement bond or rescission arrives in time, the license is suspended. CSLB warns that any work performed while a license is suspended is considered unlicensed.
Step 1: Look up your own license on the CSLB site every quarter and confirm the bond, surety and status are correct.
Step 2: Put your bond renewal and premium due dates on the same calendar as your license renewal.
Step 3: If you get a cancellation notice, call your bond agent the same day so a replacement or rescission reaches CSLB within the 30 days.
Step 4: Resolve customer and wage disputes early. A claim paid against your bond can reduce it and lead to suspension.
This is general information. For your own situation, talk with CSLB, your bond agent or a construction attorney.
Today's next step: pull up your license on the CSLB website and check that the bond listed matches your current surety.
